notes: First Q-simple, geometrically split example of [4] for the census (the gsplit cell is empty). Found by querying the LMFDB genus 2 data (devmirror.lmfdb.xyz, g2c_curves_new: is_simple_base = true, is_simple_geom = false, torsion_subgroup = [4]; geom_end_alg = Q x Q, end_alg = Q; smallest conductor among the curves of this group that the census verifier certifies). LMFDB conductor 775. Checked locally with the census's own pipeline/magma/verify_lib.m (Magma V2.30-1): J(Q)_tors = [4], class gsplit, Q-simplicity prime 3 (chi = T^4 - 2*T^2 + 9), splitness certificate: richelot over Q ((2,2)-isogenous over Q to a Weil restriction of an elliptic curve E over Q(sqrt(5)) (the surface is E x E^sigma)). Note: Magma's genus-2 Conductor on the reduced minimal model gives 793600 (2-part by Ogg's formula), not the LMFDB value 775. Submitted by F. Najman; the curve is due to the database cited under Reference. Rigorous conductor: J is (2,2)-isogenous over Q to Res_(K/Q) E with K the quadratic field of discriminant 5, so N(J) = |d_K|^2 * Norm(f_E) = 25 * 31 = 775 (computed with Magma; conductor is an isogeny invariant).
